```json
{"ranking": ["M4", "M3", "M1"], "fault": "M4 (the reference mirror output) has been shrunk to W=0.42 um, against W=2 um for M5. That cuts the mirrored current to about 0.2x. With so little bias current, M2 cannot source enough current to balance M1, so M1 pulls vout down to about 0.02 V and the gain collapses."}
```

This is a ranking from inspecting the netlist; no circuit was re-simulated. The output sitting at 0.02 V means the PMOS pull-up is far too weak compared with M1. M4 is the obvious suspect because its width (0.42 um, the minimum) doesn't match its mirror partner M5 (2 um). M3 is second because it sets the M2/M3 mirror ratio and so also controls the pull-up current. M1 is third because an oversized input device would also drag the output low. The low measured power (about 86 uW) fits a starved bias current.
